chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has wealth with another man as a loan, so he gives him something from his profit, fearing that he might cut that off from him, so he takes his wealth without it having been stipulated upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that, as long as it is not a stipulation.'
ai.seo_question: Is giving extra profit on a loan considered usury if not stipulated?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the distinction between conditional and voluntary gifts in loan transactions, a key nuance in Shia fiqh to prevent the subtle forms of riba found in commercial practices. This ruling emphasizes that the absence of a prior stipulation (shart) preserves the permissibility of the extra payment, distinguishing it from interest-based lending. The principle underscores the importance of intent and contractual clarity in Islamic finance, ensuring that gifts remain genuine acts of generosity rather than obligatory returns.
